domain: Labor Economics / Regulatory Policy / Public Administration
topic_summary: Analysis of state occupational licensing statutes as a contested kernel where professional boards read the same legal text as necessary public safety coordination (Rope) while marginalized workers and market entrants read it as rent-seeking labor suppression (Snare). The statutory mandate remains fixed while generating structurally opposite constraint types depending on interpretive commitment.

key_entities: State occupational licensing statute (legal kernel establishing credential requirements)
Professional licensing boards (interpret and enforce statutory requirements)
Marginalized workers / market entrants (excluded by credential barriers)
key_tensions: Public safety rationale vs rent-seeking suppression (boards vs entrants)
Credential requirements as quality signal vs artificial barrier (incumbent protection vs market access)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: State occupational licensing statute establishing mandatory credential requirements for market entry in a regulated profession
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Professional boards claim interpretive legitimacy through claimed expertise and delegated state authority; entrants claim legitimacy through market access rights and anti-monopoly principles

readings.commitment: Statutory credential requirements exist to prevent consumer harm through minimum competence standards
readings.authority_grounding: Professional expertise / delegated state police power
readings.expected_structural_delta: Rope: consumers in beneficiary set, incompetent practitioners in victim set; coordination around shared quality threshold

readings.commitment: Statutory credential requirements exist to restrict labor supply and extract rents for incumbent practitioners
readings.expected_structural_delta: Snare: incumbents in beneficiary set, entrants and consumers (via higher prices) in victim set; artificial scarcity extraction

readings.commitment: Statutory credential requirements create tiered market access where differential barriers sort by class and prior resource access
readings.expected_structural_delta: Snare: credentialed class in beneficiary set, marginalized workers without credential-acquisition resources in victim set; structural exclusion mechanism

axiom_contradictions.basis: Public safety reading holds consumer protection as legitimate state interest requiring credential floors; rent-seeking reading holds same floors as illegitimate market restriction absent demonstrated harm. No framework can simultaneously accept credential requirements as necessary consumer protection AND as illegitimate rent extraction.

Public safety reading grounds legitimacy in competence-based exclusion (incompetent practitioners harmed); graduated access reading grounds illegitimacy in resource-based exclusion (poor workers excluded regardless of competence). No framework can hold both credential requirements as competence-neutral class filters AND as competence-based safety mechanisms simultaneously.

axes.human_readable: Public Safety Coordination (Credential Requirements as Consumer Protection)
axes.structural_delta: Statutory mandate read as coordination mechanism establishing minimum competence threshold to prevent consumer harm
axes.primary_observable: Disciplinary action rates, malpractice claims, consumer complaint frequency pre/post-licensing regime
axes.selection_reason: First reading: establishes coordination baseline where statutory kernel operates as claimed by professional boards

axes.human_readable: Rent-Seeking Suppression (Credential Requirements as Incumbent Protection)
axes.structural_delta: Statutory mandate read as artificial barrier restricting labor supply to extract monopoly rents for licensed incumbents
axes.primary_observable: Price differentials in licensed vs unlicensed markets, wage premiums for credential holders controlling for skill, interstate licensing reciprocity barriers
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: same kernel generates extractive structure with opposite beneficiary set

axes.human_readable: Graduated Access Filter (Credential Requirements as Class Stratification)
axes.structural_delta: Statutory mandate read as resource-dependent barrier sorting by prior wealth/education access rather than competence
axes.primary_observable: Demographic composition of licensed vs unlicensed workers, credential-acquisition cost burden by income quintile, occupational mobility rates for marginalized groups
axes.selection_reason: Third reading: surfaces class-stratification dimension invisible in binary safety/rent-seeking frame

axes.structural_delta: State-by-state variation in credential requirements creates geographic mobility barriers for licensed workers
axes.primary_observable: Interstate migration rates for licensed vs unlicensed occupations, reciprocity agreement coverage, relicensing cost burden
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: derivative of coordination reading; lower structural priority than class-stratification axis

axes.structural_delta: Professional boards incrementally expand credential requirements beyond statutory minimum through rulemaking authority
axes.primary_observable: Credential hour requirements over time, examination pass rates, new subspecialty certifications
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mechanism axis rather than reading; captured via board enforcement in selected readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: State-specific credential barriers to geographic mobility
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Derivative mechanism of coordination reading; lower structural priority than class-stratification dimension

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Board-driven inflation of credential requirements beyond statutory minimum
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Implementation mechanism rather than foundational reading; captured through board enforcement analysis in selected readings

omegas.description: At what demonstrated consumer harm rate does the public_safety_coordination reading's legitimacy claim become empirically sustainable? Absent measurable harm reduction, does the coordination Rope collapse into the rent_seeking Snare?
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction between public_safety_coordination and rent_seeking_suppression

omegas.description: Do credential requirements actually measure competence, or are they resource-access proxies? If the latter, graduated_access_filter reading undermines public_safety_coordination's foundational claim even when harm reduction is measurable.
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction between public_safety_coordination and graduated_access_filter

omegas.description: Do licensing regimes produce net welfare gains when consumer protection benefits are weighed against worker exclusion costs? Trade-off depends on which reading's victim set dominates the social welfare function.

Are professional boards structurally captured by incumbent interests (supporting rent_seeking reading) or do they operate as neutral competence arbiters (supporting public_safety reading)? Board composition and incentive structure determine which constraint type the kernel actually instantiates.
omegas.source: Authority grounding divergence; Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Would voluntary certification (market signal) vs mandatory licensing (legal barrier) produce equivalent consumer protection with lower exclusion costs? If yes, mandatory structure reveals rent-seeking rather than safety motivation.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — certification alternative not addressed in kernel

fracture_scan.notes: Clean scan. Kernel structure confirmed: same statutory text generates structurally opposite constraint types (Rope vs Snare) depending on reading commitment. Three readings selected capture coordination/extraction/stratification topology. Deferred axes document implementation mechanisms without adding independent structural dimensions.
